Use Tier 2: add learned relative-position attention biases to MaskedSASRec, focusing on model_design and the corresponding predictor loading. The 1024-negative experiment reduced macro HR@10 from 0.580 to 0.565, so retain the better observed 256-negative objective and test a representation change. The hypothesis is that absolute positional embeddings alone do not adequately express how strongly an interaction’s relevance depends on its distance from the prediction query; the existing results do not establish this as the cause of the plateau.

Add a trainable signed relative-distance bias table for each attention head in each Transformer block. For each query–key pair, add the indexed bias to the attention logit before softmax, preserving bidirectional attention and the existing padding mask. Retain absolute positional embeddings, query-mask construction, auxiliary masking, tied item embeddings, jointly trained item bias, and the current loss weighting. This single architectural addition lets attention learn recency and relative-order preferences directly while retaining the successful masked-history paradigm.

Keep training seed 42, supplied splits, preprocessing seed 0, optimizer, sampling, dimensions, stopping rules, and epoch defaults unchanged. Update architecture metadata and the predictor writer so validation and host inference execute the identical modified network, loading exactly one selected checkpoint per category. Evaluate against the 0.580 reference using the pinned host’s macro HR@10 across all four categories, with 200 validation users, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42; report actual GPU cost and category scores without assuming a gain. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, and all category routes, with no hidden-test access, external weights, independently fitted scorers, or checkpoint averaging.
